en: So now that I got a server up and running, I
can use the public IP and you should have
such an IP no matter which provider you were
using. And I'll go back to my terminal
and then use the SSH command, which also is
available on macOS and also modern Windows.
And I will connect to root, which is the
default username on Hetzner and it should be
the default username for most server
providers, but that of course could differ
and you should check the official docs for
different providers to find out how their
default user is named. For AWS, for example,
their docs tell us that the default
usernames for different operating systems
are different. For example, if you chose the
Amazon Linux operating system, the default
username is ec2-user.
For Ubuntu there, it would be ubuntu.
But for Hetzner, it's root and then you add
an@ symbol after the username and then your
IP. So the username may be different, It may
be EC2-user if you were using Amazon,
but thereafter you add the IP.
Now, if I just hit Enter like this,
typically you'll be asked if you want to
essentially continue connecting even though
that's an unknown host because I never
connected to it before.
But if I choose yes here,
you'll see I'll be asked for a password
thereafter,

key. And I didn't even set any password when

wanna do
is I wanna connect but using my key. And you
do that
by adding the
-i flag for identity,

VPS course,

public key. So it will check if my private

that's the case, the connection will be
established. On Windows, you would choose
your Windows path here, which I showed you
before.
And with this command, you see that works.
Now I'm in, I see some overview here, the

and now I'm connected here still in the
terminal,
but now
to my VPS. So now any commands I run here
are no longer executed on my Mac or on your
Windows machine, but instead on that remote
device, on that remote VPS.
And that's where we'll now continue in the
next section where we'll configure this VPS
